scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000: "bir milyar"; CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000: "bir trilyon": the word for 10^12 is the short-scale 'trilyon', and 10^9 has its own word.

space_groups.source: ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in tr as "1.234.567,89": the groups take '.', so a space between digit strings separates two numbers.

fraction_agreement.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_grammar.wikitext): "When a numeral is used with a noun, however, the plural suffix is usually not used": the noun after a count stays singular, and so does a part word ('üç çeyrek').

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_grammar.wikitext): "When a numeral is used with a noun, however, the plural suffix is usually not used"; so CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000: "bir milyon" and CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "iki milyon" use the same scale word.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Turkish has no definite article, and a fraction noun alone names one part. TDK Güncel Türkçe Sözlük, "çeyrek" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/tr-ceyrek/sources/tr-tdk-ceyrek.json): sense 1 "Dörtte bir", with the example "o çeyrek ekmeği"; sense 4 "On beş dakikalık zaman"; the compounds include "çeyrek saat".

plural_scale_needs_count.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_grammar.wikitext): "When a numeral is used with a noun, however, the plural suffix is usually not used": no plural scale word is listed.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "yirmi beş": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 125: "yüz yirmi beş": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2500: "iki bin beş yüz": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "bin beş yüz"; CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "bin yirmi".

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF tr data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2010: "bin yüz", "iki bin on": the hundred or ten after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred or ten multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2500: "iki bin beş yüz" writes no comma between two classes. No source opened shows one, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "bin yirmi": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: Only the last word of an ordinal takes the ordinal suffix: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-ordinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "yirmi beşinci".

dotted_i.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish alphabet" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_alphabet.wikitext): "Dotted and dotless I are distinct letters in Turkish such that ⟨i⟩ becomes ⟨İ⟩ when capitalised, ⟨I⟩ being the capital form of ⟨ı⟩."

joiner.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "yirmi beş": no conjunction joins the parts of a number.

decimal_marker.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2.5: "iki virgül beş"

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF tr %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of -5: "eksi beş"; Wiktionary, "eksi" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-tr-eksi.wikitext): "minus"; "being negative or zero rather than positive"; Wiktionary, "negatif" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-tr-negatif.wikitext): "less than zero"

minus_idioms.source: No idiom puts the minus word before a positive number.

article_one.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_grammar.wikitext): "The cardinal number bir (\"one\") can be used as an indefinite article."

of.source: No word multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: No word stands between a fraction and a collective.

class_noun.source: No class noun follows a collective.

half_unit.source: The half word comes before the unit ('yarım kilo').

abbreviation.source: No number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: The comma is the decimal mark (CLDR 48 tr), so ',5' is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary, "arasında" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-range-arasında.wikitext): "{{head|tr|postposition}}"; "between": the word for 'between' is a postposition after the numbers, so no word before a range opens it
